getEpochRewards(uint64).details: Total BLEND reward credited across `epoch`'s committee, for an off-chain APR basis.      Read-only; DELEGATECALL'd from Staking's view forwarder.

settleEpochStipend(uint64,address,addres.details: Deps are passed as PARAMS because immutables are unreachable under DELEGATECALL.      There is no finality gate any more. The retired one read      `LivenessSlashing.lastFinalizedEpochP1()`, a cursor that existed because participation was      accumulated across a window and only became meaningful once the window closed. Payment no      longer depends on any liveness metric — it is flat by stake — and the caller is the close      of the very epoch being settled, so nothing arrives late.      Two contracts survive it: (1) settle CONTIGUOUSLY from the cursor, so a skipped or failed      settle auto-heals at a later call instead of forfeiting the epoch — which the tolerant      stipend leg makes a legal state; (2) the cursor advances ONLY past an actually-settled      epoch, so a replay is a no-op that never re-draws the reserve.

settleEpochStipend(uint64,address,addres.notice: Settle the per-epoch BLEND stipend: for every unsettled epoch up to `epoch`, compute         flat-by-stake shares over the committee and its FROZEN weights, draw them from the         reserve, and credit the ledger. Called via `Staking.settleEpochStipendFrom`, driven by         the liveness predeploy's epoch close.

documentation.text:
@dev Bound the per-call contiguous catch-up so a large finalized gap can never exceed the block
      gas limit; a wider gap simply heals over the next calls (the cursor advances by <= this each
      time and later settle(epoch) calls carry it forward).
      Sized against the MEASURED cost of one settled epoch (~2.4M gas at 51 members) and
      the hardcoded 30M system-call ceiling the whole epoch close must fit inside. At 32
      a full catch-up extrapolates to ~77M, i.e. 2.5x over the ceiling — and because an
      out-of-gas reverts the loop's cursor writes along with it, NO partial progress
      survives, so a backlog past ~11 epochs could never be worked off at all: every
      attempt died in the same place, with one warning per block as the only symptom.
      At 4 the worst case is ~9.6M inside a 12M caller bound, and a 32-epoch backlog
      clears over 8 closes instead of never.

@dev The three DELEGATECALL deps threaded through the catch-up loop, bundled into one memory
      pointer so the loop frame stays under the stack-slot limit (they are unreachable immutables).

documentation.text:
@dev BLEND stipend shares: FLAT pro-rata by STAKE, UNCONDITIONALLY.
      Everything that made payment depend on a liveness metric is gone — the participation
      floor, and with it the `belowFloor`/`partition` dual that had to exist only because the
      floor did. Payment is deliberately de-coupled from the production verdict: the tier's
      consequence is temporary EXCLUSION, never a pay cut, so a member that failed its epoch is
      still paid for the stake it had at risk. That also removes the farm vector the dual
      defended against, structurally rather than by a second guard.
      `stakes` are the weights FROZEN at commit from the selection epoch — the same vector the
      leader lottery drew with, so payment and the verdict read one committed source and cannot
      disagree about a member's weight. `pot` balance-clamps to the reserve. The only
      exclusions left are structural: a permanent equivocation tombstone, and zero weight.
